DEFINITIONS

*Medical Emergency - any situation that presents a life
threatening situation if not treated immediately

*First Aid - immediate, temporary care given to a
person in distress until before regular/specialized
medical care is available

*Note: First Aid is not restricted to physical but
also involves psychological support as well

UNIVERSAL PRECAUTIONS IN FIRST AID

Follow universal precautions, which are actions taken to
prevent the spread of disease by treating all blood as if it
were contaminated:

* Wear protective gloves when treating a victim

* Use a face mask or shield when giving first aid

for breathing emergencies.

* Cover any open wounds on your body with

sterile dressings.

* Avoid touching any object that had contact

with the victim’s blood.

* Always wash your hands thoroughly after
ng first aid.

Golden Rules of Emergency Care
What to do:

- Obtain consent, whenever possible.
- Think the worst.
- Call or send for HELP.
- Identify yourself to the victim.
- Provide comfort and emotional support.
- Respect victims modesty and physical privacy.
- Care for the most serious injuries first.

Golden Rules of Emergency Care

What not to do:

- Do not try to arouse an unconscious victim

*Do not remove penetrating objects

*Do not try to give anything by mouth to an
unconscious person or one with serious
injuries

*Do not let the victim see his own injury

*Do not leave victim except to get HELP

*Do not assume that the victim’s obvious
injuries are the only ones.

Reassurance

*One of the most important things you can do
to help the casualty is to give them
reassurance

*Keeping the casualty and yourself calm will
help as much as medical treatment

*You may also need to reassure relatives and
bystanders

After the incident, take time to tell everyone
involved how important their contribution was,
even if the outcome was unsuccessful

Stress

After an incident, a first aider may have an
emotional reaction.

*Can appear immediately after an incident, or
months later

*Signs: Frequent crying, Difficulty sleeping,
Anger, Apathy, Increased drinking or drug use,
Fear and anxiety, Flashbacks, Headaches,
Stomach problems, lack of appetite, Sadness
and depression

*Get professional help if does not resolve
